BACHELOR THESIS PROJECT

Design and Construction of an Engine Test Bench for Automotive Diagnostics and Fault Simulation

Bachelor Thesis · Applied Mechanical Engineering – Automotive Maintenance and Diagnostics

ISET Nabeul · Tunisia

Back to Portfolio

Project Overview

As part of my bachelor thesis, a fellow student and I designed and built an educational test bench using a decommissioned Opel Astra G 1.2 ECOTEC combustion engine.

Objectives

The aim was to build a mobile teaching model that enables students to carry out the following practical exercises:

  • Explore the structure and operating principles of an internal combustion engine.
  • Diagnose compression loss and combustion chamber leakage.
  • Remove and install the timing chain.
  • Adjust and independently verify valve timing.
  • Identify engine management sensors and actuators.

Technical Implementation

01

Disassembly and Refurbishment

Complete disassembly of the engine, cleaning of individual components using a parts washer, high-pressure cleaning and sandblasting, followed by painting.

02

Valve Lapping and Leak Testing

All valves were lapped except the intake valves of cylinder 2 and the exhaust valves of cylinder 3, deliberately leaving potential sealing defects.

Diagnostic principle

Apply compressed air to the valve port and observe the wetted valve seat. Bubbles reveal leakage.

Technical schematic · not to scale
03

Piston Ring Fault Simulation

The top compression ring of cylinder 4 was deliberately shortened to increase its end gap and simulate air leakage past the piston rings into the crankcase.

Students compare cylinder pressures using a compression test kit while cranking the engine. Cylinder 4 is expected to show reduced pressure.

Why compression drops

Technical schematic · not to scale

A larger ring gap provides an additional leakage path toward the crankcase.

Fault map — expected diagnostic findings

CylinderSimulated fault
1Reference cylinder without an intentional fault
2Leaking intake valves
3Leaking exhaust valves
4Increased top compression ring end gap
04

Engine Reassembly

Replacement of selected wear parts, reassembly of engine components, installation of the timing chain and adjustment of valve timing.

05

Electrical Verification of Valve Timing

Design of an electrical verification circuit with two position contacts on the crankshaft and exhaust camshaft. An LED indicates when both shafts simultaneously reach their intended alignment positions.

06

Fabrication of the Engine Stand

Fabrication of a mobile steel frame by cutting and arc welding, with an integrated engine mount, battery shelf and four casters.

Project Outcome

A decommissioned, non-functional combustion engine that had been sitting unused in the university workshop was transformed into an educational model with a new purpose. Instead of discarding the engine, we gave it a new lease of life by converting it into a hands-on training system.

Students can work on a real combustion engine, perform fault diagnosis and practise disassembly and reassembly. This allows them to develop practical skills and confidence without the fear of causing irreparable damage to a working engine.
